solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One replacing heads in hierarchy drastically scaled back (5)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows
the phrase is cut down at both ends, leaving only the letters in the middle

blocks.note: the letters run across the join: the last two of the first word and the first three of the second

annotation.surface: An organisation replacing its bosses cuts its management layers back hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like company bosses, but it means literal heads: the Hydra grew new ones as fast as Hercules cut them off.
annotation.definitionFit: The Hydra of Greek myth replaced each severed head with two more.

entries.clue: Obscure end eg Dina had? (6,6)

indicators.note: to obscure the letters is to disguise them by jumbling their order

blocks.note: twelve letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A question about some woman called Dina and the secret goal she was pursuing.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read plainly, an obscure end that Dina had is a hidden agenda, and the same words supply the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a concealed aim, an end kept obscure from others.

entries.clue: Was hanging out drawers at first on damp clothes line (5)

indicators.note: only the first letter of drawers is used
WET clothes L, wrapping round it
in a down clue, D sits on top of the rest

blocks.note: first letter of drawers
damp means wet
L is the standard abbreviation for line; it goes inside WET

annotation.surface: Someone was pegging out underwear on a washing line while it was still damp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hanging out' is slang for living somewhere, not laundry on a line; the washing picture is all misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live somewhere; hanging out is a casual way of saying the same.

entries.clue: Unexpectedly kiss lad near a girl (9)

indicators.note: the letters turn up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter
taken letter for letter into the mix with X

annotation.surface: A boy standing near a girl suddenly kisses her.
annotation.walkthrough: The X for kiss joins the anagram fodder rather than being added afterwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: Alexandra is a girl's first name, the Greek form meaning defender of men.

entries.clue: Hurts hip making contact with panels (8)

blocks.note: hip and in both mean fashionable
a jury is a panel

annotation.surface: A patient complains that their hip hurts where it touches some panels.
annotation.walkthrough: Hip looks like the joint, which suits 'Hurts'; it is the adjective meaning trendy.
annotation.definitionFit: Hurts as a plural noun, the harms suffered, are injuries.

entries.clue: Hype up travelling by plane involving great speed (6)

indicators.note: IN JET involves C, taking it inside

blocks.note: in a jet
c is the speed of light, the greatest speed there is

annotation.surface: Hype builds for a trip on a very fast aircraft.
annotation.walkthrough: Hype is the drug slang: a hype is a hypodermic, so to hype up is to inject.
annotation.definitionFit: To hype up, in drug slang, is to inject oneself with a needle.

entries.clue: Judge I deceived lives close to devout religious campaigner (8)

indicators.note: the close of devout is its last letter

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
as printed
to be had is to be fooled
he is, i.e. he exists
last letter of devout

annotation.surface: A judge admits being fooled by someone living next to a pious zealot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but it means the close, the last letter, of devout.
annotation.definitionFit: A jihadist is someone waging jihad, a religious struggle or campaign.

entries.clue: Blame papers: Express, particularly? (5)

blocks.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
identity papers

annotation.surface: Pointing the finger at the press, in particular the Daily Express newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: With 'papers' next to it, Express looks like the tabloid; it is an express train, whose defining quality is speed.
annotation.definitionFit: An express, particularly, is rapid: speed is what makes a train or delivery express.

entries.clue: All the day before Rosemary extremely on edge (5,4)

indicators.note: before in time, so the day's letters are placed ahead of Rosemary's
only the extreme letters of Rosemary are used
in a down clue, the first part sits on top of INCH

blocks.note: the eve is the day before, as in Christmas Eve
first and last letters of Rosemary
to edge forward is to inch forward

annotation.surface: Rosemary has been nervous all through the day before some event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous, but 'on' places the parts and edge is a verb meaning inch.
annotation.definitionFit: Every inch means all of something, as in every inch a king.

entries.clue: Song opener recalled in study, lavatory and shed (3,3,4,4)

indicators.note: called back, i.e. read backwards, so KEY becomes YEK
in means inside, so the reversed opener is placed within the study

blocks.note: a key opens a lock; reversed to YEK
a den is a private study; YEK goes inside
john is slang for lavatory
to peel is to shed a skin

annotation.surface: Someone remembers the first line of a song while sitting in the study, the loo and the garden shed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Song opener' wants to be the definition, since the answer is the song's first line; 'Song' alone is the definition and opener gives KEY. D'ye Ken John Peel is an old English hunting song from Cumberland; ken means know.
annotation.definitionFit: D'ye Ken John Peel is a traditional hunting song about a Cumberland huntsman.

entries.clue: One used to stir from one’s laptop so rarely (7,5)

indicators.note: in a rare, unusual fashion, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: twelve letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone who seldom manages to get up from their laptop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like getting moving; it is stirring a cup. An apostle spoon is a silver spoon with a figure of an apostle on the handle, a traditional christening gift in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: an apostle spoon is a teaspoon, the kind of implement used to stir a cup.

entries.clue: Did transport lobby finish off road? (9)

indicators.note: the finish of road is its last letter

blocks.note: a lobby is an entrance hall
last letter of road

annotation.surface: A question about whether the transport lobby group got a road scheme finished.
annotation.walkthrough: Transport and lobby both suggest the politics of roads; transport is the verb meaning delight, and lobby is a hallway.
annotation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with delight, so to entrance is to transport.

entries.clue: Work in kitchen? / Say no more! (3,2)

blocks.note: drying up is wiping the washed dishes
a curt exclamation telling someone to stop talking

annotation.walkthrough: To dry up is British for drying the dishes after washing up.
annotation.definitionFit: Drying up is a kitchen chore, and to dry up is also to stop talking.

entries.clue: In disagreement when accepting Fleet Street offer? (2,4)

indicators.note: AS accepts TODD, taking him inside

blocks.note: as and when both mean at the time that
Sweeney Todd, the murderous barber of Fleet Street, was an offer: one who offs, or kills, people

annotation.surface: Arguing over whether to accept a newspaper's deal, Fleet Street being the old home of the London press.
annotation.walkthrough: Offer is not a bid but a joke noun: one who offs. Fleet Street is a London street long synonymous with newspapers, and in legend home to Sweeney Todd.
annotation.definitionFit: Odds once meant differences between things, so to be at odds is to be at variance, disagreeing.

entries.clue: Alternatively, however, perform unknown numbers in straight line? (9)

blocks.note: or offers an alternative
tho is short for though, i.e. however
to do is to perform
x and y are the unknowns in algebra

annotation.surface: Some mathematical instruction about plotting unknown values along a straight line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Straight line' suggests geometry; it means the strict line of accepted belief, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Orthodoxy is the straight, correct line of doctrine; orthodox literally means right belief.

entries.clue: Son in sports car calls for middle gear (1-7)

indicators.note: in means inside, so the son sits within the sports car

blocks.note: a GT, gran turismo, is a sports car; S goes inside
S is the abbreviation for son
to ring is to phone, i.e. call

annotation.surface: A son driving a sports car rings up asking for mid-range gear.
annotation.walkthrough: Middle gear suggests the car's gearbox; it is clothing worn round the middle of the body.
annotation.definitionFit: G-strings are skimpy garments covering only the middle of the body, gear for the middle.

entries.clue: Men rising presumably no longer hold back in dance (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so OR becomes RO

blocks.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
a made-up word: if to delay is to hold back, to undelay would presumably be to stop doing so

annotation.surface: Men getting up to dance, no longer holding back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' flags that UNDELAY is not a real word, just a plausible coinage.
annotation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a simple song with a refrain, and also a dance in a ring.

entries.clue: Eccentric chap primarily inducing anxious state (8)

indicators.note: only the first letters of inducing and anxious are used

blocks.note: an eccentric is a cam, an off-centre wheel in machinery
bod is British slang for a person, a chap
first letters of inducing and anxious

annotation.surface: An odd fellow makes people nervous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Anxious state' reads as a mood; state is a country. Eccentric looks like an adjective (or an anagram signal), but here it is the engineering noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a state in South-East Asia.

entries.clue: Special preserve of former prince in time married (5,3)

indicators.note: in means inside, so the prince is placed within time and married

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
T is the abbreviation for time
a raja is an Indian prince; he goes between T and M
M is the abbreviation for married

annotation.surface: A special keepsake from a one-time prince, married in his day.
annotation.walkthrough: Preserve suggests something kept; it is the fruit spread. Extra jam is a UK labelling term for jam with a higher fruit content.
annotation.definitionFit: Extra jam is a legally defined grade of jam with more fruit, so a special preserve.

entries.clue: What can be missed, contained briefly here? One’s light? (6)

blocks.note: a bus can be missed
held, i.e. contained, cut short

annotation.surface: A puzzled query about what might have been missed and where someone's light might be.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the biblical saying 'hide one's light under a bushel', not to show off one's talents: the bushel is where one's light goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A bushel, a measuring basket, is where the proverb says one's light is hidden.

entries.clue: Answer nothing in court cases around recess (6)

indicators.note: LOVE cases C, enclosing it

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
love is nil in tennis scoring, on court
c, circa, means around; it goes inside LOVE

annotation.surface: No answer given in court cases round about the time of a break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court cases' is not a legal phrase: court belongs with nothing (tennis), and cases is the container verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an alcove is a nook set back into a wall.

entries.clue: Returned case carrying yellow flag (5)

indicators.note: the whole is turned back, read right to left
something carrying a load holds it, so the case holds yellow within it

blocks.note: a pod is a seed case
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

annotation.surface: A package sent back with a yellow flag on it.
annotation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a banner, fitting yellow; it is the verb meaning to tire or wilt.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: flag as a verb means to tire and sag, as wilting flowers or spirits do.

entries.clue: After games, lay out English tea (5)

blocks.note: PE, physical education, is school games
to lay someone out is to knock them out, KO
E is the abbreviation for English

annotation.surface: After sport, setting out an English tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lay out' suggests setting the tea table; here it means flooring someone with a punch.
annotation.definitionFit: Pekoe is a high-grade black tea.

entries.clue: Levels of nonsense drop off, alas, only at the end (9)

indicators.note: just the end letter of alas is used

blocks.note: bull is slang for nonsense
to drop off is to doze
last letter of alas

annotation.surface: The amount of nonsense falls away, sadly only towards the end.
annotation.walkthrough: Levels looks like a noun, amounts; it is the verb, to flatten.
annotation.definitionFit: To bulldoze is to level ground or buildings.

entries.clue: Priest having a party in the middle of blitzkrieg (5)

indicators.note: in means inside, so the party is placed within the middle letters
the two central letters of blitzkrieg

blocks.note: a do is a party
blit(ZK)rieg: the middle two of its ten letters

annotation.surface: A priest throws a party in the thick of a bombing raid.
annotation.walkthrough: Zadok is the priest who anointed Solomon in the Bible, known from Handel's anthem Zadok the Priest.
annotation.definitionFit: Zadok was a high priest of Israel in the time of David and Solomon.

entries.clue: Drew pair of spectacles on bird — a crow (4-1-6-3)

indicators.note: in an across clue, DOODLED OO goes on after COCK A

blocks.note: a cock is a male bird
as printed
doodled, drew idly
two round lenses look like OO

annotation.surface: Someone sketched glasses onto a picture of a bird, a crow.
annotation.walkthrough: Crow looks like the bird named in the picture; it is the verb, the rooster's call.
annotation.definitionFit: Crow here is the noun for a rooster's call, and this is how English spells that call.

entries.clue: Baskerville maybe kind and brave (4-4)

blocks.note: a kind is a type
to brave a danger is to face it

annotation.surface: Praise for a Baskerville as gentle and courageous.
annotation.walkthrough: Baskerville calls up the Hound of the Baskervilles; it is a typeface designed by John Baskerville.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by maybe: Baskerville is one serif design, created by John Baskerville in the 1750s.

entries.clue: I don’t like that about remote place (5)

blocks.note: yuk! expresses disgust
on, as in a talk on a subject, means about

annotation.surface: Someone expresses distaste at a faraway location.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole opening phrase is one exclamation giving YUK.
annotation.definitionFit: The Yukon is a sparsely populated territory in north-west Canada.
